title: Shaving or trimming
hookLine: men shave or trim, women cut a fingertip's length

cards: "And those who trim?" It's the companions asking. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has just asked God to have mercy on those who shave their heads.
Some of the men listening have only trimmed theirs. So they ask: and those who trim? He repeats the prayer for those who shave.
They ask again. Only after asking more than once do they hear him include them: and those who trim. A small, almost funny exchange, people making sure they're counted.

teach.b: Start with why hair matters here at all. In ihram, pilgrims don't cut their hair; Surah Al-Baqarah tells them not to shave their heads until the offering has reached its place.
Then, after the stoning and the sacrifice, it's cut.

Anas reports in Sahih Muslim that the Prophet came back to his place at Mina, called the barber, pointed to one side of his head and then the other, and gave his hair away to the people. Second, the two ways.
The hadith from the hook, in Sahih al-Bukhari, praises those who shave, and when asked, includes those who trim. Both are allowed for men. Shaving is the fuller act; trimming is enough.
A report from Ibn Abbas in Sunan Abi Dawud says women don't shave; they only shorten.
Jurists describe it as cutting about a fingertip's length from the ends. Fourth, what the cut does. It marks a release.

Much of what ihram held back is lifted, and the pilgrim can wear ordinary clothes again. Surah Al-Fath pictures believers entering the Sacred Mosque in safety, heads shaved and hair cut, without fear. One more thing.
On that busy day people did the rites in a jumble, and came to the Prophet worried. One said he'd shaved before sacrificing.
The answer, in Bukhari: do it, there's no harm. The schools of law later discussed when a change of order needs making up. But that day, the worried were met with ease.
So the end of ihram is something anyone can see: a shaved head, or hair a little shorter at the ends.

how: After the stoning and the sacrifice, male pilgrims shave their heads or trim their hair and women cut a small length from the ends, which releases them from most of the restrictions of ihram.

games.q: it's the day of sacrifice and the rites got out of order: you shaved before your animal was sacrificed. you go to the Prophet, worried. what does he say?
o: go back and start the day over.
games.why: in Bukhari, asked about rites done early or late that day, he answers: do it, there's no harm.

practice: Turn your hands over and look at your nails, growing all this time without any help from you, the way a pilgrim's hair grows through ihram.

Let them stand for the stretch you've just come through, this week, this season, and ask whether something in it is finished. If you pray, say a quiet bismillah for what comes next; if not, just breathe.

wordCard.voice: Shaving or trimming. Men shave or trim their hair, and women cut a little from the ends, marking the release from ihram. Today's word.

orig.note: shaving the head; trimming is taqsir.
